note: Majority: the Family Law (Porodični zakon, Sl. glasnik RS 18/2005 as amended), article 11: majority at eighteen; full capacity also by a court-allowed marriage before majority, or by court leave for a parent of sixteen (not held). Work: the Labour Law (Zakon o radu, Sl. glasnik RS 24/2005 as amended to 109/2025), article 24: employment with a person of at least fifteen; article 25: under eighteen only with a parent's or guardian's written consent and a health finding. The law makes no exception for performers below fifteen, so the form holds them barred (my reading: a child's performing engagement outside employment isn't held). Service: the Law on Military, Labour and Material Obligation (Zakon o vojnoj, radnoj i materijalnoj obavezi, Sl. glasnik RS 88/2009, 95/2010, 36/2018) still sets a six-month term from the year a man turns 19 (articles 24 and 25), but the consolidated text, whose 2010 amendment (95/2010) applies from 1 January 2011, speaks of voluntary service 'after the suspension of compulsory service' (posle obustave obaveze služenja vojnog roka; which article enacted the suspension wasn't found in this text); women aren't conscripted. Service is none. Registration (regrutna obaveza) from the year of 18 and reserve duty to 60 aren't held. Press found by a search on 2026-10-31 (not read) reports a planned 75-day service for men, not yet law as of mid-2026; it isn't modelled. Texts read from Paragraf.rs, a private legal publisher's consolidated texts.
